licences: Required to take any saltwater fish, Fla. Stat. § 379.354(1), unless a § 379.353(2) exemption applies. Spearfishing is fishing. The free resident shoreline licence, § 379.354(4)(k), covers fishing "from land or from a structure fixed to the land" only; FWC states it is not valid for taking by swimming or diving, so a diver entering from shore needs the full licence. Carry it in personal possession while taking or possessing fish, § 379.354(3). Scuba divers aboard a dive boat that carries them for a fee and holds the right vessel licence are not required to hold individual licences, § 379.354(7)(f). Spiny lobster needs the separate annual lobster permit, § 379.354(8)(d).

R. 68B-5.006(2) exempts taking lionfish while diving with a hand net, pole spear, Hawaiian sling or a lionfish-specific spear from the licence requirement. No bag or size limit. The rebreather harvest ban has an exception for lionfish only.

FREE and annual, separate from your licence, r. 68B-14.009. Required to harvest or possess these while aboard a vessel in Florida waters: almaco jack, banded rudderfish, greater and lesser amberjack; gray triggerfish; black, gag and red grouper; hogfish; mutton, red, vermilion and yellowtail snapper. A diver who enters from shore is outside the trigger. The rule was amended 1 Sep 2026 without changing this; the amendment adds a separate Atlantic For-Hire Reef Fish Registry (2026 to 2028) that owners or operators of vessels for hire must join. Whether a dive charter counts is not settled: ask FWC, 850-487-0554. The 65-and-over licence exemption does not exempt you.

Fla. Stat. § 327.331: a face mask and snorkel makes you a "diver", so freediving counts. Stay within 100 ft of the device in rivers, inlets and navigation channels and 300 ft elsewhere. The flag is at least 12 by 12 in shown from the water and 20 by 24 in shown from a boat, § 327.331(1)(c)1. Other boats inside those distances must slow to headway speed, § 327.331(6). The flag must come down once every diver is aboard or ashore, and a boat may not run with it up unless divers are in the water, § 327.331(7).
statewide: The four buffers: r. 68B-20.003(2)

"Except as provided in Rule 68B-20.004, F.A.C., spearfishing is hereby prohibited" within 100 yards of all public bathing beaches, 100 yards of commercial or public fishing piers, 100 yards of any bridge where public fishing is legally permitted, and 100 feet of the unsubmerged portion of any jetty. Note the unit change on jetties. On this map the jetty buffer is drawn at 75 structures statewide, the bridge buffer along each deck that the NOAA chart or the Census road map shows, the pier buffer around every FWC-listed pier, and the beach buffer along the open-coast sandy beaches that FDEP's range monuments mark. Beaches on bays and lagoons, and piers and bridges missing from the inventories, are not drawn: assume all four apply wherever there is a beach, pier, fishing bridge or jetty.
Bridges: unless FDOT has investigated and posted a ban, the buffer applies

Fla. Stat. § 316.1305 makes fishing from a bridge lawful unless FDOT investigates, finds it dangerous, and posts signs. All three steps are required. So an unposted bridge falls within the rule's words 'where public fishing is legally permitted', and the 100 yd spearfishing buffer attaches. Limited-access facilities (Interstates, toll expressways) bar pedestrians, so no buffer attaches there. There is no statewide register of posted bridges. Separately, jumping or diving from any publicly owned bridge is prohibited, posted or not, Fla. Stat. § 316.130(17). On this map each coastal and tidal bridge buffer is drawn along the deck where the NOAA chart or the Census road map shows one, not only around the inventory point; where neither shows a deck, only the circle is drawn and a long bridge is under-drawn.
State park waters: r. 68B-20.003(2)(e), r. 62D-2.014(9)(d)

Spearing prohibited in any water under the DEP Division of Recreation and Parks. Spear gear may only be aboard if not loaded and properly stored in a vessel passing nonstop. Does NOT reach federal parks or the National Estuarine Research Reserves. Twelve parks that adjoin water are not yet drawn (among them Navarre Beach, St. George Island, Amelia Island and Estero Bay); treat water beside any state park as closed.
Statutory closed areas: § 379.2425
John Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park, and the Upper Keys from the Miami-Dade/Monroe county line south through Long Key. Collier is in the statute but FWC reopened it by r. 68B-20.003(1)(a).
Florida Keys sanctuary

50 of the 76 FKNMS zones prohibit fishing entirely, spearfishing and freediving included. Carrying a speargun or pole spear in the Key Largo and Looe Key Management Areas is itself an offence unless in uninterrupted transit, 15 C.F.R. § 922.164(b)(1)(iv). 25 of the 50 are in state waters, where the 2025 Restoration Blueprint does not apply because the Governor objected; the 1997 zoning controls there, backed by Florida's own rr. 68B-6.002 and 68B-6.003(1)(b). Confirm with FKNMS, 305-809-4700.
Western Dry Rocks (Key West): seasonal closure

All fishing, spearfishing included, prohibited 1 April to 31 July in the state waters of the box, r. 68B-6.004. Transit only with spear shafts out of the gun. The rule lapses after 31 Mar 2028 unless FWC renews it.
Gear-list closures: Old Tampa Bay, Turkey and Crane Creeks

Two rules name the only gear allowed and leave spears off the list. Old Tampa Bay north of the Gandy Bridge, including every creek and bayou emptying into it: hook and line, landing or dip net, cast net, permitted crab and shrimp traps, r. 68B-25.003(2). Turkey Creek and Crane Creek (Palm Bay and Melbourne) west of their mouths: the same list without shrimp traps, r. 68B-3.009. Both are closed to spearfishing and gigging.
Volusia County: r. 68B-3.008

In Volusia inland salt waters the rule prohibits spearing any species except flounder and sheepshead, and limits the gear to a barbed spear of three prongs or fewer. The rule does not define inland salt waters; assume the whole Halifax River and Mosquito Lagoon system. A state rule, not a county ordinance.
Lobster and crabs

No spear, hook or other device that could puncture or crush a lobster, r. 68B-24.006(10); federal waters too, 50 C.F.R. § 622.404(a). No lobster at any time in the Biscayne Bay-Card Sound Spiny Lobster Sanctuary, and nobody may be in the water there from a boat carrying lobster, rr. 68B-11.001, 68B-11.003 and 68B-11.004. Pennekamp: no lobster in the two-day sport season, and in the regular season none in seven buoyed zones or on any patch reef, r. 68B-24.0065 (seven zones since 1 Jul 2026). Stone crab and blue crab may not be speared, r. 68B-13.008(1), r. 68B-45.004(1).
Monroe County canals

No discharging a speargun in any manmade canal in unincorporated Monroe County, Monroe County Code § 26-5. The City of Marathon has its own ban on firing a speargun in manmade canals, City Code § 18-27 (read 30 Sep 2026). Around the lobster seasons, Monroe County Code § 26-98 bars diving and snorkeling in any manmade water body or marina and within 300 ft of improved residential or commercial shoreline, from three days before the mini-season through the first five days of the commercial season, in incorporated and unincorporated Monroe County (read 7 Oct 2026; not drawn).
Local ordinances

County and city codes in 141 coastal jurisdictions were searched on 30 Sep 2026. Whole-city bans: Venice ("within or near" city waters), Cedar Key (gigs included), St. Pete Beach and Treasure Island (discharging a speargun), Bal Harbour (firing a band, spring or air spear in village waters), Lauderdale-By-The-Sea (loading a speargun), Dania Beach (spear gear on the beach or in the water) and Sunny Isles Beach (fishing by spear in the Atlantic except in designated areas). Larger structure buffers and inlet closures in Lake Worth Beach, City of Sarasota, Melbourne, Boca Raton, Pompano Beach, Marco Island and John's Pass. County park waters closed to spears in Lee, Hillsborough, Brevard and Manatee. Browser reads on 7 Oct 2026 added Hollywood (no spearfishing within 100 yards of the public beach, drawn), Pinellas County (no spearing in any manmade saltwater canal), Naples (no swimming within 100 ft of a public bridge), Town of Palm Beach (no fishing off or within 50 yards of a guarded beach), Deerfield Beach (no swimming beyond 50 yards of the city beach without lifeguard permission) and St. Petersburg (no fishing in park waters unless signed); they are in the citation registry and not yet drawn. Every local rule is treated as live. See the county notes. Added 8 Oct 2026: Clearwater bans firing any spring, air or gas projectile weapon citywide, spearfishing excepted only where designated (§ 21.06), drawn closed like Treasure Island. Canal gear rules like Pinellas County's also cover Cape Coral and Sanibel (special acts), listed Naples and Collier canals, unincorporated Brevard and named Satellite Beach canals: hook and line, cast nets or crab traps only. Preemption: Fla. Stat. § 379.2412 reserves saltwater fishing regulation to the state except for fishing from property a local government owns; § 790.33 covers firearms, not spearguns. Until a court says otherwise, obey the local rule.
National parks

Dry Tortugas NP: spearfishing prohibited park-wide, weapons broken down and stowed, 36 C.F.R. § 7.27; the Research Natural Area in the northwest 46 square miles is closed to all fishing and anchoring. Everglades NP: only a closely attended hook and line, § 7.45(d)(6). Gulf Islands National Seashore: the 2021 Superintendent's Compendium banned pole spears, spear guns, Hawaiian slings and any other projectile device in all Seashore waters. The compendium updated 1 Sep 2026, read in full on 7 Oct 2026, has no spearfishing or projectile rule, so the park adds no spear closure of its own and Florida's rules apply (36 C.F.R. § 2.3(e)). Fishing is closed at the Fort Pickens and Ship Island ferry docks, the Davis Bayou boat ramp dock, the Ship Island boardwalk and the designated swim beaches while lifeguards are on duty, and diving is prohibited within 200 ft of the Fort Pickens fishing pier. Two stale nps.gov pages still print the 2021 ban: call the park at 850-934-2600 to confirm it was rescinded. Seashore water runs one mile from the low tide line at Perdido Key, Fort Pickens and Santa Rosa, and 100 yards at Naval Live Oaks. Biscayne NP: no federal regulation found bans spearfishing park-wide; state law governs. Closures researched: Legare Anchorage (no diving at all), within 100 ft of any marked channel, three harbors, and the bonefish box from 1 March to 31 May, r. 68B-7.008(5). Canaveral NS: vessels may not operate or anchor within 500 ft of the ocean shoreline. In every park unit a speargun is a weapon (36 C.F.R. § 1.4), and a loaded weapon is prohibited in any vessel, anchored or under way, § 2.4(c): unload before you climb back aboard. Park fresh waters are hook and line only, § 2.3(d)(1). Gear and catch that are illegal in Everglades NP may cross it only by Indian Key, Sand Fly, Rabbit Key or Chokoloskee pass, § 7.45(d)(9).
National wildlife refuges

50 C.F.R. § 27.21 bars taking any animal on a refuge unless part 32 opens it. Opened refuges with a rule that bites: Hobe Sound (rods and reels and poles and lines only), Pinellas (fishing only from vessels around Tarpon Key), Egmont Key (two attended poles), each excluding spearing on the conservative reading; Ding Darling (no spears from Wildlife Drive); Ten Thousand Islands (no spears in the freshwater and brackish marsh); Cedar Keys (300 ft around Snake Key closed to all entry 1 March to 30 June); Merritt Island (refuge fishing permit). Passage Key and Crocodile Lake are closed to the public. Key West and Great White Heron are not opened in part 32, but FWS's own pages say fishing and diving in their waters are governed by state law. The conflict is unresolved. 50 C.F.R. § 27.43 also prohibits using or possessing spears and gigs on any refuge unless a refuge rule authorizes it. Crystal River NWR: no fishing in refuge waters (FWS), drawn closed.
Manatee zones: state No Entry and federal sanctuaries

A state No Entry zone bars "all vessels and all persons, either in vessels or swimming, diving, wading, or fishing", r. 68C-22.002(11): 20 zones in 9 counties, most at power-plant canals (the Vero Beach power-plant zone in Indian River County became Idle Speed all year on 30 Jun 2026 and no longer bars divers); Biscayne Bay west of Virginia Key is closed all year. Motorboats Prohibited zones do not bar divers. At the 11 federal sanctuaries (seven in Kings Bay, Blue Waters on the Homosassa, and the Bartow, Big Bend and Port Sutton sites in Tampa Bay) "All waterborne activities are prohibited" 15 Nov to 31 Mar, 50 C.F.R. § 17.108(a). The federal sanctuaries are not drawn.
Military areas: 33 C.F.R. part 334

Florida has 42 danger zones and restricted areas (§§ 334.500 to 334.780): Eglin, Tyndall, NAS Pensacola, NSA Panama City, KSC and Cape Canaveral, Patrick, MacDill, Mayport, Blount Island, Key West. Some are closed at all times (MacDill, the Coast Guard facilities at Mayport, Miami Beach and Destin, the Key West naval areas, NAS Pensacola, NAVSTA Mayport). Most offshore ranges close only when active. Off Dania Beach and John U. Lloyd, § 334.580 bans anchoring or attaching anything to the bottom over the reef tract at all times; the rule does not prohibit drift diving. Anywhere in Florida, no vessel or person may come within 100 yards of a large U.S. naval vessel, 33 C.F.R. § 165.2025.
Port and security zones: 33 C.F.R. part 165

Fixed zones close water to vessels and persons without Captain of the Port permission at Tampa Bay (port facilities, power plants, MacDill; no dive operations under the Sunshine Skyway main span), Port Canaveral, NAS Jacksonville, Port Everglades and the Miami Main Channel, Sector Key West, and the three Mar-a-Lago zones (the Atlantic East zone has been no-entry since 5 Sep 2025, when enforced). At the Port of Palm Beach there is no fixed port zone: the zones move with, or sit 100 yards around, passenger and hazardous-cargo vessels from the Lake Worth sea buoy in. Kennedy Space Center waters close on launch days, § 165.701.
Federal fishery areas (EEZ)

Spearfishing gear prohibited at the Ft. Pierce Inshore Reef and Key Biscayne / Artificial Reef H SMZs, 50 C.F.R. § 622.182 (the Ft. Pierce Offshore Reef SMZ rule does not ban it). Warsaw Hole spawning SMZ west of Key West: no snapper-grouper by any gear and no anchoring by fishing vessels until 2 Aug 2027, § 622.183(a)(2). Oculina experimental closed area (27°30′ to 27°53′ N, 79°56′ to 80°00′ W): no snapper-grouper, § 622.224(b)(2). North Florida, St. Lucie Hump and East Hump MPAs: no snapper-grouper, § 622.183(a)(1). Gulf: Madison-Swanson, Steamboat Lumps and the Tortugas reserves closed to all fishing; The Edges closed January to April.
Federal gear rules

In the Gulf stressed area a powerhead may not be used on reef fish, § 622.35(a); that rule does not restrict spearguns. In the South Atlantic EEZ a diver on a rebreather may not spear snapper-grouper, § 622.180(b). Highly migratory species: a speargun only for bigeye, albacore, yellowfin and skipjack tuna, from a boat with an HMS Angling or Charter/Headboat permit, § 635.21(h); never billfish, swordfish or sharks. King mackerel and Atlantic Spanish mackerel: a spear is not on the federal gear list, § 622.375(a)(1); the map treats spearing them in federal waters as not authorized. For dolphin and wahoo in Atlantic federal waters the gear rule does not exclude spears or powerheads, § 622.272(a)(1); in state waters powerhead harvest is prohibited.
Fresh water

Spearfishing is prohibited in all Florida fresh water, and spearguns may not even be possessed there. R. 68A-23.002(7): the use or possession of spear guns "in or upon the fresh waters of the state" is prohibited, so a speargun aboard a boat on a freshwater river is a violation. The Steinhatchee River is fresh water by statute from source to mouth, § 379.101(17).
Powerheads, bangsticks, rebreathers
No powerhead harvest in state waters, and no harvest on a rebreather except lionfish, r. 68B-20.003(7). The rule does not bar carrying a powerhead for protection.
Keep the fish whole

Reef fish must be landed whole: no fillets, heads off or skin off on the water, a pier, a fishing bridge or a jetty; gutting and removing the gills are not prohibited, r. 68B-14.006(4). In federal waters every Gulf finfish and every South Atlantic snapper-grouper keeps head and fins, 50 C.F.R. §§ 622.10(a), 622.186(a). A boat harvesting reef fish in state waters, spearfishing included, must carry a venting tool or rigged descending device, r. 68B-14.005(3).
prohibited:
Spearing prohibited by r. 68B-20.005: billfish · sturgeon · tarpon · bonefish · goliath grouper (the rule still says "Jewfish") · Nassau grouper · permit · Florida AND African pompano · all sharks · spotted eagle ray · manta and devil rays · snook · red drum · spotted seatrout · weakfish · tripletail · and the families surgeonfish, trumpetfish, angelfish and butterflyfish, porcupinefish, cornetfish, squirrelfish, trunkfish, damselfish, parrotfish, pipefish and seahorses, and puffers.

Barred by other rules: spiny lobster, r. 68B-24.006(10) · stone crab, r. 68B-13.008(1) · blue crab, r. 68B-45.004(1) · every triggerfish and filefish except gray triggerfish, ocean triggerfish and unicorn filefish: these are marine life species that may be taken only with nets and slurp guns, rr. 68B-42.001(2)(bb) and 68B-42.007 (read on a secondary copy).

Goliath: a limited hook-and-line permit harvest exists, but spearing is always prohibited, r. 68B-14.005(7); federal waters are closed to all harvest. Tripletail is barred twice: r. 68B-20.005(17) and r. 68B-49.006, which reaches federal waters. Sharks: hook and line only, r. 68B-44.006(1). Federal waters: a speargun may be used only on bigeye, albacore, yellowfin and skipjack tuna among highly migratory species, 50 C.F.R. § 635.21(h); Nassau grouper, speckled hind and warsaw grouper may not be taken in the South Atlantic EEZ, § 622.181(b).
seasons: Read this first

Values below were checked on 7 Oct 2026. Seasons move by FWC executive order and federal temporary rule; check FWC and NOAA before every trip. Where a date comes from an FWC notice or news release rather than the text of an order or rule, it says so.
Gag

24 in TL. Atlantic state waters, including all of Monroe, and South Atlantic federal waters: closed from 2 Aug 2026 to 30 Apr 2027 (FWC EO 26-10 to 31 Dec, then r. 68B-14.0039(2); 91 FR 21389, then 50 C.F.R. § 622.183(b)(1)). The 2027 closing date has not been set. Gulf state waters (not Monroe) and Gulf federal waters: closed from 1 Oct 2026 to 31 Aug 2027 (EO 26-26 to 31 Dec, then r. 68B-14.0039(1); 91 FR 29920, then § 622.34(e)). From 28 Oct 2026 the South Atlantic federal private vessel limit is 2 gag and black grouper combined per day (91 FR 61160, Regulatory Amendment 36); Atlantic state waters and all of Monroe, from 28 Oct 2026: 1 gag or black grouper per person, and no more than 2 gag or black grouper combined aboard any vessel at any time, charters included (r. 68B-14.0036(2)(b)1.).
Red snapper

Atlantic, state and federal waters: closed outside 9 to 22 Oct 2026; 1 fish, no minimum size, hook and line, bandit gear, handline or spear only, trip declaration required (FWC EO 26-33, read from the order). Federal waters close at 12:01 a.m. 12 Oct 2026 except on Florida exempted-fishing-permit trips, which run to 22 Oct (91 FR 60334). A December season is possible but not announced. Gulf, private vessels, state and federal waters (FWC notice, secondary): closed 5 to 8 Oct, 26 to 29 Oct, 2 to 6 Nov, 9 to 13 Nov, 16 to 20 Nov, 23 to 25 Nov, 30 Nov to 4 Dec, 7 to 11 Dec, 14 to 18 Dec, 21 to 24 Dec and 28 to 31 Dec 2026, and from 5 Jan 2027 until FWC announces the 2027 season. 16 in TL, 2 fish.
Hogfish

Atlantic and Keys (and Gulf waters south of 25°09′ N), state and federal waters: closed 1 Nov to 30 Apr every year; in 2026 to 2027, closed 1 Nov 2026 to 30 Apr 2027. r. 68B-14.0042 and 50 C.F.R. § 622.183(b)(4). 16 in fork, one fish. Gulf north of 25°09′ N: 14 in fork, 5 fish, no closed season.
Shallow-water grouper

Atlantic and all Monroe waters: gag, black, red, scamp, yellowfin, yellowmouth, red hind, rock hind, coney and graysby closed 1 Jan to 30 Apr, r. 68B-14.0039(2). 3-grouper aggregate in the Atlantic and Monroe, 4 in the Gulf. From 1 Jan 2027 Gulf federal waters are closed to black grouper, scamp, yellowfin and yellowmouth grouper from 1 Jan to 30 Jun every year (50 C.F.R. § 622.34(h), 91 FR 36545). The Gulf federal closure beyond 20 fathoms (1 Feb to 31 Mar) was removed effective 2 Oct 2026 (91 FR 63502). The Edges stays closed to all fishing 1 Jan to 30 Apr. South Atlantic federal waters: no more than 1 scamp or yellowmouth within the 3 grouper, 50 C.F.R. § 622.187(b)(2)(v).
Greater amberjack

Atlantic: 28 in fork, 1 fish, closed in April. Gulf: 34 in fork, 1 fish; state and federal waters closed from 14 Oct 2026 to 31 Aug 2027 (FWC EO 26-25 to 1 Nov 2026, then r. 68B-14.004(1); federal temporary rule 91 FR 32360 to 31 Jul 2027, then 50 C.F.R. § 622.34(c)).
Flounder
14 in TL, 5 per day; the rules do not exclude spear as gear. Closed 15 Oct to 30 Nov every year, r. 68B-48.005, in state and federal waters: in 2026, 15 Oct to 30 Nov 2026.
Snowy grouper and tilefish

Snowy grouper closed in Atlantic state waters (FWC EO 26-18, from FWC's announcement) and South Atlantic federal waters (91 FR 32906) from 7 Jun 2026 for the rest of 2026. Golden tilefish closed in South Atlantic federal waters 27 Mar to 31 Dec 2026 (91 FR 14651).
Snapper

Mutton 18 in TL. Gray 10 in state / 12 in federal waters. 10-snapper aggregate. Biscayne National Park has larger minimums and a 10-fish park aggregate, rr. 68B-7.003 and 68B-7.004. South Atlantic federal waters: of the 20 other snapper-grouper, no more than 10 of any one species, § 622.187(b)(8).
Cobia
36 in fork. 1 per person, 2 per vessel. The rules do not exclude spear as gear in state or federal waters.
Mackerel

In state waters the rules do not exclude spear as gear. In federal waters a spear is not on the gear list for king mackerel or Atlantic Spanish mackerel, 50 C.F.R. § 622.375(a)(1); the map treats spearing them there as not authorized. For Gulf Spanish mackerel the federal gear rule does not exclude spear.
Puffer fish
Take prohibited in Martin and St. Lucie counties, r. 68B-3.007. Spearing puffers is prohibited everywhere by r. 68B-20.005.
Prohibited outright

Goliath grouper: spearing always prohibited; a hook-and-line permit harvest (1 Mar to 31 May) exists outside Martin to Miami-Dade. Nassau grouper, speckled hind and warsaw grouper: no harvest. Snook: hook and line only, and a snook may not be aboard with spear gear, r. 68B-21.006(3). Tarpon: no spearing in or out of state waters, r. 68B-32.006(2).
safety: No recompression chamber in Palm Beach County
Nearest: South Florida Center for H.O.P.E., Deerfield Beach, 954-571-9392, and Mercy Hospital, Miami, 800-662-3637 (1-800-NO-BENDS).
Narrowest shelf on the US East Coast. The Gulf Stream sets north essentially always. Live-boat drift with a competent operator on the surface.
State waters end at 3 nm on the Atlantic, 9 nm on the Gulf
Beyond that line federal rules apply: South Atlantic Council off the east coast and the Atlantic side of the Keys, Gulf Council off the west coast.
ramps: $15/day + tax or $50/yr + tax ($53.25) since 1 Oct 2025, all six county saltwater ramps. The fee fields inside FWC's dataset are stale.

In Palm Beach only Phil Foster and Burt Reynolds have 24-hour county access, 24-hr max, and the permit does not allow overnight storage. Paid overnight trailer parking: Lake Park Harbor Marina, ~$44/night.
Closed since 2 Sept 2025 for redevelopment, reopening spring 2027.
Florida has none; ramp access is entirely county or municipal. Ramps whose name contains 'PERMIT REQUIRED' need a local decal.

Palm Beach.txt: The only county with live spearfishing special acts. PBC Code App. G ch. 13 art. II. From Laws of Fla. ch. 59-1702 (§§ 13-31 to 13-39): no underwater spearfishing in any county salt water from one hour after sunset to one hour before sunrise (§ 13-32), none at any time within any inlet in the county, Jupiter, Lake Worth, South Lake Worth (Boynton) and Boca Raton (§ 13-33; drawn at Jupiter, Lake Worth and South Lake Worth inlets, the broader reading of 'inlet'; Boca Raton Inlet is also closed by the city), diver-flag rules (§§ 13-36 to 13-38) and a 150 ft standoff from anchored boats (§ 13-35); these reach freedivers too. From ch. 59-1699 (§§ 13-54 to 13-59): no sale of speared fish (§ 13-58) and two refuge areas where spearfishing on underwater breathing apparatus is prohibited (§§ 13-55, 13-56). FWC repealed three other PBC fisheries acts in r. 68B-3.038 and left these two standing. Treat as live law. Town rules (read 30 Sep 2026): Lake Worth Beach, no skin diving or spearfishing within 500 ft of the ocean, Snook Island and Bryant Park piers; Lantana, spearguns banned on the municipal beach and in its waters; Boca Raton, no diving in Boca Raton Inlet or near the Palmetto Park Road bridge; Delray Beach, no scuba from the municipal beach; Juno Beach, no loaded speargun on the beach or pier; Lake Park, no diving in the Harbor Marina. Mar-a-Lago security zones: Center and East (Atlantic) zones no-entry when enforced. South Palm Beach, Manalapan and Tequesta: no spear rule found (30 Sep 2026). Town of Palm Beach (read 30 Sep 2026): § 74-161 bars spearfishing gear on five named public beaches including Phipps and Midtown and requires guns to be carried uncocked on other Town beaches; § 74-200 sets buddy, certification, BC and flag requirements for diving off guarded beaches. Read 7 Oct 2026: § 74-162(e) bars fishing in the waters off any guarded Town beach and 50 yards north or south of it, and § 74-197 bars swimming more than 300 ft from mean low water off a guarded beach (not drawn). Boynton (South Lake Worth) Inlet also bans swimming in the inlet and entering it from the jetties, bulkheads or bridge, and closes the ocean within 75 ft of the sand transfer plant, or its area of influence if larger (§ 18-1). Town of Palm Beach § 74-162(b) also bars fishing from town bridges and docks and the town areas under them.

Martin.txt: No live spearfishing special act. Puffer fish take prohibited (r. 68B-3.007). Stuart, Jupiter Island and Sewall's Point codes have no spear rule (pier and bridge diving rules only). Hobe Sound NWR allows only rods and reels and poles and lines, which excludes spearing; St. Lucie Inlet Preserve State Park water is closed. Offshore, the St. Lucie Hump MPA bans snapper-grouper. Anchoring on reef or colonised hard bottom carries civil penalties, § 403.93345. Martin County code: no spear rule found in a whole-code search (30 Sep 2026; repeated 7 Oct 2026 across the code, the land development regulations and the comprehensive plan). The old fish and wildlife chapter 83 was repealed on 21 Oct 2025; chapter 83 now limits saltwater fishing from county bridges to one pole.

Saint Lucie.txt: No live spearfishing special act; FWC repealed 57-1791. Puffer fish take prohibited (r. 68B-3.007). Fort Pierce: fishing, defined to include spears, banned at eight listed places including Moore's Creek and the city marina waters, and no propelling a spear in any city park area. Federal: the Ft. Pierce Inshore Reef SMZ bans spearfishing gear; the Ft. Pierce Offshore Reef SMZ rule does not ban it; the Oculina experimental closed area offshore bans snapper-grouper. Harbor Branch waterway is a manatee No Entry zone all year. Fort Pierce Inlet State Park water is closed. County code negative; Port St. Lucie and St. Lucie Village not read.

Broward.txt: No live spearfishing special act. City rules: Dania Beach bans spear gear on the beach and in the water and all diving within 100 yards of the Ocean Park pier; Lauderdale-By-The-Sea bans loading a spear gun anywhere in town and diving within 300 ft of the pier; Hallandale Beach, no spearfishing or scuba on the public beach except in a designated area (none in the code); Pompano Beach, nothing within 100 ft of the pier and no diving in part of Hillsboro Inlet; Deerfield Beach, no snorkeling within 50 yards of the pier, no swimming more than 50 yards off the city beach without the lifeguard's permission, and no fishing off the beach from 8 a.m. to dusk (§ 50-112(b), (p), read 7 Oct 2026). Hollywood: § 99.03(F), spearfishing is prohibited within 100 yards of the public beach, which runs from the Hallandale line to John U. Lloyd Beach State Park and 50 yards offshore; loaded spearguns are barred on the beach and in public swimming areas (read 7 Oct 2026; drawn 175 yards from the chart coastline, the 150 yards of the rule plus margin). freshwater: The test is a taste test: there is no salinity number

Fla. Stat. § 379.101(33) defines salt water as all Florida territorial water excluding lakes, rivers, canals and other waterways "from such point or points where the fresh and salt waters commingle to such an extent as to become unpalatable because of the saline content." Note the words: the test is unpalatability alone. The phrase "and unfit for human consumption" belongs to the fresh water definition and is routinely misattached to this one. No parts-per-thousand threshold, no conductivity figure and no chloride limit exists anywhere in Florida fisheries law. Only the Steinhatchee River has a designated boundary. Other states did not solve it either: Mississippi, South Carolina and Louisiana all use geography (I-10, US 17, the Intracoastal Waterway), not salinity. Louisiana's legislature said why: salinity is "insusceptible of precise location by reason of the changes in water salinity caused by winds, tides, and rains."
"Brackish" is not a legal category
Florida recognises exactly two: fresh and salt. Brackish water is legally one or the other, decided by the palatability test.
Only one river is legally designated
The Steinhatchee: the statute declares it fresh "from its source to mouth." Every other water body is left to the commingling test, or to a commission order that appears never to have issued.
There is no official fresh/salt map

Verified negative. FWC publishes no per-river boundary list and no GIS layer. Their own guidance sidesteps it: "License requirements follow the species of fish, regardless of where they are caught." Any inland/coastal line on this map is inference, not a copied boundary.
Spearfishing in fresh water: two separate bans

R. 68B-4.012(3): no harvesting any marine species by hand or mechanically propelled spear or lance "while diving in fresh water." R. 68A-23.002(7) (in force since 7 Jun 2022): the use or possession of spear guns "in or upon the fresh waters of the state" is prohibited unless a rule or permit allows it.
Possession of a speargun on fresh water is itself prohibited

CORRECTED 8 Oct 2026. This item used to say FWC overstated the rule. It did not: r. 68A-23.002(7), read verbatim on 7 Oct 2026, prohibits the "use or possession" of spear guns "in or upon the fresh waters of the state". A speargun aboard a boat on a freshwater river or lake is a violation even if nobody dives. The earlier text relied on an older numbering of the rule.
Why fresh-water rules treat bowfishing and spearfishing differently

The line is the water's surface, not the spear. R. 68B-20.002: gigging is deployed at or above the surface; spearfishing is operated by a person swimming at or below it. Fresh water permits manually operated spears, gigs, bows and crossbows from a boat or shore, for nongame fish only. Spearguns are banned regardless.
Licensing and gear rules do not reconcile

Licensing is species-based; the spearfishing ban is water-based. Holding the right licence for the species is no defence to the water-based gear ban, and vice versa. The combination licence costs about $1.50/yr more than a single, so there is no reason not to hold both.
"Inland salt waters" is never defined

The phrase appears repeatedly, including in Volusia's R. 68B-3.008, and is bounded only by reference to ocean beaches and inlet jetties. It is a subset of salt water used for county gear overlays, not a third category.
What to do when it is genuinely unclear

In a tidal river, a mangrove creek, or anywhere behind a salinity structure, the regime can move with season, drought and tide. The cautious reading is the conservative one: if you cannot establish the water is salt, treat it as fresh, because the freshwater side is where the speargun ban lives, and it is the side with criminal exposure.
